summary: First-pass full test of BlueSeaTra BTP procurement app. Backend: 15/15 pytest passed, including calculation-correctness tests (prix_achat=8.46, marge=25, qty=10, tva=20 → 112.80 / 22.56 / 135.36 EUR ✓). Frontend: Dashboard, Catalogue (search, filter, pagination, detail dialog, add-to-panier toast), Estimateur (line calc, global TVA presets 0/5.5/10/20/custom, global marge, save/load project), Fournisseurs, Parametres pages all load and work. Nav OK. One runtime error found on /alertes when typing in the alerts-search input (TypeError: toLowerCase is not a function).

ui_bugs.issue: Uncaught TypeError: (r[k] || "").toLowerCase is not a function when typing in alerts-search. Crashes the whole Alertes page. Cause: line 15 assumes r[k] is always a string; when a filter key (article/code/lot/point_controle/nature/fournisseur) resolves to a non-string (e.g. number or object) in one of the rows, .toLowerCase() throws. Fix: coerce with String(r[k] ?? "").toLowerCase().

action_items: Fix filt() in /app/frontend/src/pages/Alertes.jsx line 15: use String(r[k] ?? '').toLowerCase() to avoid runtime crash on non-string values.

rca of the issue: Alertes.filt calls (r[k] || '').toLowerCase() over data.a_completer, data.a_verifier, data.controls simultaneously (all three TabsContent render at once). When search is non-empty, at least one row across the three arrays has a filter-key value that is not a string (likely null coerced-to-non-string, or a numeric field). Reproduction: navigate to /alertes → type any text in alerts-search → red overlay 'Uncaught runtime errors: (r[k] || "").toLowerCase is not a function'. Mitigation: change filt to `arr.filter((r) => keys.some((k) => String(r[k] ?? '').toLowerCase().includes(search.toLowerCase())))`.
